situation:
You are to assume the role of store manager at HARBOR & GRAIN POKE CO., a poke and salad counter with six locations in a coastal city. The owner (judge) has asked to meet with you about a break in the supply of the ingredient the counter is known for.

HARBOR & GRAIN POKE CO. has served build-your-own poke and salad bowls for eleven years, and the menu board promises ahi that is line-caught by LANTERN BAY FISHERIES, a family fishery two harbors away. Guests say that promise is why they choose the counter. A new competitor, BRIGHT SHORE BOWLS, opened three blocks from your busiest store this spring and has taken close to a fifth of your lunch traffic.

A boat repair has stopped LANTERN BAY FISHERIES from delivering ahi for the next three weeks. The fishery has supplied every store since the first one opened and wants the relationship to continue. A national seafood broker has offered to fill the gap at a lower price per pound, but only if the company signs a twelve-month exclusive contract.

Signing the broker's twelve-month exclusive contract would cut food cost immediately and keep the ahi bowl on the menu, but it would cost the company the line-caught promise printed on its menu board and the fishery relationship behind it. Pulling the ahi bowl for three weeks and featuring a lower-priced marinated salmon bowl would protect both, at the cost of lunch sales in the busiest weeks and of regulars who may cross to BRIGHT SHORE BOWLS.

The owner (judge) wants you to compare the two courses and recommend one, and to explain how each would affect the guests who choose the counter for its fish. The owner (judge) will begin the role-play by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the owner's (judge's) questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of owner of HARBOR & GRAIN POKE CO., a poke and salad counter with six locations in a coastal city. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the store manager (participant) to compare the broker's twelve-month exclusive contract against pulling the ahi bowl for three weeks, and to recommend one course. You want to hear what each course would cost the company, and how guests who come for the line-caught ahi would be treated at the counter while the supply is short.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If we had gone the other way, what would that have cost us?
What would our regular guests notice about the choice you did not recommend?
